metadata.name: SparkEngine
metadata.description: A source-first C++23 game-engine project under active release hardening, with an inspectable runtime, editor, tools, modular games, and server-authoritative multiplayer foundations.

hero.title: Build worlds.
hero.lede: SparkEngine brings a multi-backend rendering architecture, EnTT ECS, Jolt physics, an ImGui editor, modular games, and server-authoritative multiplayer work into one inspectable codebase. Its readiness is defined by evidence and release gates—not feature-count marketing.
trust: Every maturity claim linked to evidence

overview.title: A broad engine. Every boundary visible.
overview.copy: SparkEngine began around FPS needs and expanded into editor workflows, runtime modules, dedicated servers, asset tooling, large-world foundations, and reference games. The repository now records what is implemented, how it is verified, what is supported, and what still blocks a release.
overview.grounding: The current strongest route remains Windows, C++, and D3D11. That is a candidate path, not a production-readiness certificate; each declared profile's required gates and applicable work remain authoritative.

pillars.title: One abstraction, unequal backend maturity
pillars.copy: D3D11 is the primary path. D3D12, Vulkan, OpenGL, Metal, and NullRHI are described independently so implementation depth is never confused with support or release status.

pillars.title: Runtime systems share one source tree
pillars.copy: ECS, Jolt physics, animation, navigation, audio, assets, persistence, job execution, and modular games can be inspected and tested together.

pillars.title: Authority is designed into the runtime
pillars.copy: Transport, replication, prediction, reconciliation, lag rewind, dedicated-server execution, and Area/World coordination exist, while public-service security and operations remain explicit work.

pillars.title: The workbench is part of the product
pillars.copy: SparkEditor sits beside the console, shader compiler, build tooling, launcher, installer, crash reporter, profiler, and validation utilities. End-to-end authoring and shipping gates determine readiness.

referenceGame.name: TERRAFRONT
referenceGame.label: MMOFPS reference module
referenceGame.title: A combined-arms engineering vertical slice
referenceGame.lede: The MMOFPS module is the deepest in-repository proof that rendering, simulation, UI, persistence, vehicles, territory, and networking can meet in one game. It is a reference implementation, not evidence of a shipped public MMO service.

features.title: Playable proving ground
features.copy: Factions, classes, weapons, vehicles, deployables, territory, squads, bots, HUD, map, and account flow exercise the module boundary.

features.title: Server-authoritative validation
features.copy: Movement and fire validation, rate budgets, finite-value checks, weighted violations, and kick escalation provide concrete security entry points.

features.title: Prediction and reconciliation
features.copy: Shared movement, quantized state, owner reconciliation, interpolation, unchanged-state suppression, and hit rewind form the gameplay network loop.

features.title: Local persistence reference
features.copy: Accounts, characters, unlocks, loadouts, territory, and progression demonstrate a local pipeline that still needs a transactional service design for production use.

referenceGame.boundary: This module proves substantial vertical integration. It does not prove secure public hosting, distributed production shards, operational scale, transactional persistence, abuse controls, or commercial release readiness.

showcases.title: Dockable tools, one authoring surface
showcases.copy: A repository capture of the editor panel system and its scene, asset, profiler, server, and content-authoring surfaces.

showcases.copy: A repository capture of the experimental collaboration lane, including presence, locking, hosting, and joining.

showcases.title: Authority without a GPU
showcases.copy: A repository capture of NullRHI-backed headless execution for dedicated-server and automation paths.

showcases.title: The runtime stays inspectable
showcases.copy: A repository capture of logs, history, completion, aliases, and forwarded engine commands in the standalone console.

status.title: Know what the evidence proves.
status.copy: Implementation breadth, test coverage, supported use, and release readiness are separate dimensions. SparkEngine is source-usable today and remains blocked from a fully ready release until every declared profile's required gates and applicable work have current evidence.

quality.title: Evidence is part of the engine.
quality.copy: A large source tree only becomes trustworthy when the required builds, tests, sanitizers, packaging checks, performance budgets, and security gates fail closed and attach evidence to the exact commit.

ecosystem.title: Choose a verified path through the engine.
ecosystem.copy: Role-based paths resolve to current repository documents and source entry points, so renamed or removed guidance cannot silently linger.

ecosystem.title: Keep durable technical discussion in the ecosystem.
ecosystem.copy: Categories, threads, replies, search, profiles, subscriptions, notifications, reporting, and moderation replace GitHub Discussions without inventing activity.

ecosystem.title: Move from a question to an owned change.
ecosystem.copy: Issues, pull requests, forum work, and contribution policy point back to the current repository instead of a manually copied roadmap.

ecosystem.title: Read the controlling files before you ship.
ecosystem.copy: License, attribution, contribution, conduct, and security guidance link to the exact repository revision and never replace legal review.

ecosystem.title: Turn every blocker into verifiable work.
ecosystem.copy: Profile-required gates, dependency-ordered work items, source entry points, commands, tests, documentation changes, and promotion rules form a complete code-session handoff.

build.title: Start with a reproducible checkout.
build.copy: There is no published versioned release yet. The repository is the available distribution surface, and its release handoff lists what must pass before that changes.

commands.windows:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Krilliac/SparkEngine.git
cd SparkEngine
.\generate.bat -g "Visual Studio 17 2022" release
.\build.ps1 -config Release -editor -angelscript
commands.unix:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Krilliac/SparkEngine.git
cd SparkEngine
./generate.sh release -g Ninja
./build.sh release

readiness.title: SparkEngine Release Readiness
readiness.description: A repository-owned release-gate program and dependency-resolved implementation handoff for taking SparkEngine from source-usable to fully ready.
readiness.heroCopy: This is the engine completion program: current evidence, profile-required release gates, explicitly excluded gates, and the exact applicable work a code session can pick up next. Project-fit guidance remains available, but it now follows the same capability contract.
readiness.methodCopy: A feature can be substantially implemented and still be unverified, unsupported, or release-blocked. The site names all four dimensions and links every promotion to evidence.

choices.label: Windows
choices.note: The primary host candidate; release gates still apply.
strengths: Windows has the broadest engine, editor, and D3D11 coverage.
boundaries: A current Shipping build, installer, signing, and release evidence are still required.
choices.nextMove: Run the required Windows build-and-test gate at the target commit.

choices.label: Linux
choices.note: Build and headless foundations exist with renderer and packaging validation debt.
strengths: GCC, Clang, sanitizers, NullRHI, OpenGL, and Vulkan have repository surfaces.
boundaries: End-to-end rendering, packaging, driver coverage, and support commitments are incomplete.
choices.nextMove: Prove one packaged golden scene on the declared Linux support matrix.

choices.label: macOS
choices.note: Build work exists; Metal is not a complete production renderer.
strengths: The repository contains macOS build and platform entry points.
boundaries: Metal implementation, notarized packaging, renderer parity, and system tests remain open.
choices.nextMove: Complete the Metal backend and prove a notarized packaged golden scene.

choices.label: D3D11 client
choices.note: The primary rendered candidate on Windows.
strengths: D3D11 carries the deepest production-renderer implementation.
boundaries: Golden-scene coverage, performance budgets, packaging, and current release evidence still gate readiness.
choices.nextMove: Run the Windows D3D11 golden-scene and performance certification lane.

choices.label: Headless / NullRHI
choices.note: Purpose-built for no-render servers and automation.
strengths: NullRHI provides a real no-GPU device path.
boundaries: Soak, load, shutdown, crash, and packaged-server gates remain required.
choices.nextMove: Run the packaged dedicated-server soak and load suite.

choices.label: D3D12 / Vulkan / OpenGL / Metal
choices.note: Implementation depth varies and parity is not yet certified.
strengths: Modern and portable backend implementations provide real R&D entry points.
boundaries: Feature parity, shader toolchains, golden scenes, drivers, synchronization, and packaging need backend-specific proof.
choices.nextMove: Choose one backend and close its explicit parity gate before combining targets.

choices.label: Single-player
choices.note: Avoids the public-service layer while exercising the core runtime and tools.
strengths: The runtime, editor, save, asset, input, audio, physics, and gameplay systems can be proven locally.
boundaries: Cooked asset loading, save migration, installer, crash, performance, and end-to-end authoring gates still apply.
choices.nextMove: Ship one packaged vertical slice through the full editor-to-runtime loop.

choices.label: Controlled multiplayer
choices.note: Exercises authority and replication on known hosts.
strengths: Transport, replication, prediction, reconciliation, and dedicated-server foundations exist.
boundaries: Protocol compatibility, hostile-client testing, observability, persistence, and operations require explicit proof.
choices.nextMove: Run a versioned client/server compatibility and soak test under loss and latency.

choices.label: Public internet service
choices.note: Adds security, identity, fleet, abuse, persistence, and operational requirements.
strengths: TERRAFRONT and the network stack offer implementation references.
boundaries: Secure transport, accounts, secrets, matchmaking, fleet control, backups, moderation, telemetry, incident response, and load proof are not turnkey.
choices.nextMove: Treat the service layer as its own product program and close the production-network gate.

choices.label: C++ modules
choices.note: The primary extension and game-module path.
strengths: C++ owns the complete runtime and module boundary.
boundaries: ABI/versioning, hot reload, packaged modules, and SDK compatibility need release gates.
choices.nextMove: Prove a packaged module against the declared SDK compatibility contract.

choices.label: AngelScript
choices.note: A functional integration with runtime and workflow completion work remaining.
strengths: VM, bindings, module isolation, and entity-facing APIs exist.
boundaries: Per-frame dispatch, reload state, debugging, packaging, migration, and authoring acceptance remain open.
choices.nextMove: Close the script lifecycle and hot-reload work item with packaged tests.

choices.label: Visual scripting
choices.note: The graph/compiler surface is not yet a complete production authoring loop.
strengths: A node palette and AngelScript generation path exist.
boundaries: Validation, debugging, source mapping, migration, reload, packaging, and editor acceptance remain open.
choices.nextMove: Prove graph-to-packaged-runtime execution with diagnostics and migration coverage.

learn.title: Learn SparkEngine
learn.description: Repository-resolved learning tracks that stay aligned with the current documentation and source tree.
learn.heroEyebrow: Learning paths / generated from current docs
learn.heroCopy: Every path combines concepts, exact repository documents, source entry points, and a concrete outcome. Missing or renamed documents fail publication instead of leaving a dead tutorial behind.

tracks.label: Contribute safely

docs.title: SparkEngine Documentation
docs.description: The recursively indexed SparkEngine guides, specifications, module notes, project status, and source-derived API reference for the published repository commit.
docs.heroCopy: Every route is rebuilt from the repository documentation catalog and pinned to the source commit that produced it. Authored guidance, generated reference, status, research, and proposals retain distinct provenance labels.
docs.sourceCopy: The repository is the controlling source. A document's presence proves that it is published context—not that every forward-looking statement is implemented or release-ready.
docs.proposalNotice: Forward-looking material is rendered for engineering context and does not promote the described capability.
docs.researchNotice: Research material records investigation and options; it is not a support or release commitment.

community.title: SparkEngine Community
community.description: The first-party forum, project chat, issue tracker, pull requests, documentation, and contribution path around SparkEngine.
community.heroCopy: Questions become searchable answers. Ideas become proposals. Reproductions become issues. Focused changes become reviewed code. Each surface has a clear job and an auditable path back to the repository.

channels.label: Forums
channels.copy: Durable questions, proposals, module discussion, and show and tell.

channels.label: Discord
channels.copy: Fast coordination when an answer does not need to be permanent.

channels.label: Issues
channels.copy: Reproducible defects and accepted, scoped implementation work.

channels.label: Pull requests
channels.copy: Reviewed code, tests, documentation, and auditable contribution history.

support.title: Send the problem to the right system.
support.copy: There is no paid support desk or guaranteed service level today. Use the project surfaces that exist and keep reusable technical knowledge searchable.

contribution.title: From curious to reviewable.
contribution.copy: Contribution begins with a bounded observation and enough evidence for another person to review it.

steps.title: Improve an explanation
steps.copy: Correct or clarify a repository document and link the code that proves it.

steps.title: Reproduce a rough edge
steps.copy: Turn a vague complaint into a minimal build, editor, or runtime reproduction.

steps.title: Implement one bounded change
steps.copy: Follow the C++23 style, wire the lifecycle, add production-source tests, and update readiness evidence.

steps.title: Review and teach

ecosystem.title: Table stakes now. Infrastructure after proof.
ecosystem.copy: Website polish and operating infrastructure are different deliverables. SparkEngine labels the boundary and only promotes repository-backed services.

stages.title: Use what exists
items: First-party forum with search, profiles, saves, and moderation

ecosystem.promotionRule: Every future surface must publish its owner, maturity, evidence, data footprint, and known limitations before it earns a live label.

community.policyBaseline: The repository Code of Conduct is the effective project-wide behavior source. Forum-specific moderation and appeals require a separately maintained operating policy.

legal.title: SparkEngine Legal & Trust
legal.description: The exact-commit SparkEngine license, conduct, contribution, security, attribution, and unresolved governance status.
legal.heroCopy: SparkEngine's enforceable project documents live with the source. This overview routes readers to those documents and marks unresolved governance work instead of presenting a draft as policy.

license.name: Spark Open License 1.0
license.summary: The license grants broad commercial and non-commercial use, modification, publication, distribution, sublicensing, and sale, subject to notice, naming, anti-plagiarism, and attribution conditions.
license.disclaimer: Plain-language overview—not legal advice. If this site differs from the checked-in license text, the license text controls.

permissions.title: Use and copy
permissions.copy: Run the software and make copies.

permissions.title: Modify and merge
permissions.copy: Change the source and combine it with other work.

permissions.title: Publish and distribute
permissions.copy: Share, sublicense, or sell covered copies.

conditions: Retain the copyright and license notice in covered copies or substantial portions.
Provide visible attribution to SparkEngine and Krilliac when distributing derived work.
Do not brand a fork or modified version as SparkEngine, Spark Engine, SparkEditor, or with the SparkEngine logo without permission.
Accurate statements that work is based on or derived from SparkEngine are allowed.
Do not present a substantially unmodified copy as original work.
license.attributionTemplate: This software is derived from SparkEngine by Krilliac (https://github.com/Krilliac/SparkEngine).

legal.securityCaution: Use the repository's private advisory route when available. Do not post exploit details in a public issue, forum, or chat. Version-support and response commitments remain release-governance work until the legal/support gate passes.

Cookie notice if non-essential cookies are introduced

footer.description: A source-first C++23 game-engine project and engineering community with implementation, verification, support, and release maturity kept distinct.
